51547737.protein: Nuclear receptor subfamily 4 group A member 2
51547737.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to recombinant N-terminal His6-tagged human Nurr1 LBD (362 to 598 residues) expressed in Escherichia coli BL21(DE3)-R3-pRARE2 by ITC method

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods - Isothermal Titra: Isothermal Titration Calorimetry. ITC experiments were conducted on an Affinity ITC instrument (TA Instruments, New Castle, DE) at 25 °C with a stirring rate of 75 rpm. Nurr1 LBD protein (10 or 20 μM) in buffer (20 mM Tris, pH 7.5, 100 mM NaCl, 5% glycerol) containing 5% DMSO was titrated with the test compounds (50 or 100 μM in the same buffer containing 5% DMSO) in 21 injections (1 × 1 and 20 × 5 μL) with an injection interval of 180 s. As control experiments, the test compounds were titrated to the buffer and the buffer was titrated to the Nurr1 LBD protein under otherwise identical conditions. The heats of the compound–protein titrations were corrected with the heats of the compound–buffer titrations and analyzed using NanoAnalyze software (version 3.11.0, TA Instruments, New Castle, DE) with independent binding models.
original_paragraph.Figure 2 caption: Figure 2. Characterization of de novo designs 7 and 8 as Nurr1 agonists. (a,b) ITC demonstrated high-affinity binding of 7 (a) and 8 (b) to the Nurr1 LBD. The upper panels show the isotherms of the compound–protein titrations and the lower panels show the fitting of the blank-corrected heat of binding. (c,d) 7 and 8 induced mRNA expression of the Nurr1-regulated genes TH and VMAT2 in T98G astrocytes. Data are shown as mean ± S.E.M., n = 4. *p < 0.05, **p < 0.01, ***p < 0.001 (vs DMSO-treated cells; ANOVA with Bonferroni correction).
original_paragraph.Figure 2 panel a: Kd = 0.14 μM, n = 0.95, ΔH = -39.3 kcal/mol, TΔS = -30.3 kcal/mol
original_paragraph.Figure 2 panel b: Kd = 2.4 μM, n = 1.07, ΔH = -28.0 kcal/mol, TΔS = -20.4 kcal/mol

assay_conditions.control_method: Titration of test compounds into buffer and buffer into Nurr1 LBD protein; heats of compound–protein titrations corrected with heats of compound–buffer titrations
